page: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v6 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine configuration with expanded memory allocation. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processors operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz. The hardware profile provides 4 physical cores running 1 thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Processing is supported by extended vector and cryptography instructions, including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16), VAES, and SHA-NI.

The system provisions 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage via Azure Premium Storage volumes. In synthetic execution tests, the high CPU clock speeds yield strong top-tier single-core results, registering 3080.88 in stress-ng single-core tests and 2108.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations. Multi-core performance scales predictably across the 4 dedicated cores, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 6842.0 and 12287.35 in stress-ng.

Memory subsystem benchmarks reveal 592.54 GB/sec throughput for cached small-block reads, though uncached large-block reads decline to 38.92 GB/sec. Text generation for lightweight 135M language models executes rapidly at 270.12 tokens per second, but prompt ingestion drops considerably on larger 7B parameter architectures. The absence of local solid-state drives and discrete hardware accelerators limits intensive local IOPS and massive AI training. However, the high per-core RAM density coupled with dedicated AMD execution units offers solid resource efficiency for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise application runtimes, and moderately scaled compilation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v6 is a specialized virtual machine configuration providing 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9V74 processors running at 3.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an expanded 32.0 GB of RAM, granting 8.0 GB of memory per core. The processor features AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) along with 32 MB of L3 cache, delivering strong single-thread execution in Geekbench (2108.0) and stress-ng (3080.88). The instance contains no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistent data. Large-block memory reads exhibit moderate latency penalties, but cached operations and multi-threaded decompression perform reliably. With its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and dedicated core mapping, the instance is functionally suited for in-memory caching solutions, Redis data stores, software build orchestration, and enterprise web services requiring sustained per-core compute power.
